# tgrep runtime

Ash builds tgrep 1.1.0-ash.b614b8c.4 from upstream commit `b614b8c51e76607abffaf73239c42365f0e3c1ff`. [`runtime-lock.json`](runtime-lock.json) fixes the source archive, [`ash-runtime.patch`](ash-runtime.patch), and the shared [ranking](../../crates/file-search/src/ranking.rs) and [directory admission](../../crates/file-search/src/discovery.rs) sources by SHA-256. This includes the seven upstream commits after `e9d55db`: indexed-read containment and source-byte limits, search compatibility fixes, error chaining, Windows release compatibility, and shared-runtime qualification and performance coverage. Review source and protocol differences before changing the pin.

- Source, patch and shared-source SHA-256 values are checked before applying or compiling. Cargo uses `--locked`; build caches are keyed by source, patch, both shared sources, toolchain and target and verify the resulting binary digest.
- Compilation uses a temporary source and target directory, removed on success or failure. The cache retains only the executable, its digest manifest and the build lock. Reusing a verified executable also removes its legacy compiler target directory under the same lock.
- Development, release and Remote packages use the same resolver. Builds require Rust and Git; searches do not download or compile the runtime.
- Packages retain `ash-resources/tgrep/tgrep[.exe]` and the upstream MIT license.
- `ash-tgrep` supervises upstream `serve --shared` and owns each worktree lease. Ordinary directories, unborn repositories and directory subroots use upstream single-directory `serve`. Search correctness, base generations, admission, watchers and delta checkpoints belong to tgrep.
- The Ash patch supplies the packaging version, `identity` command, path-ordered global `max_results` (1–5001), a shared status file count, consistent candidate statistics and error code `-32002` for invalidated/not-ready snapshots. Permanent errors retain `-32001`. Ash reconciles only the readiness errors within the original request deadline.
- Path-mode attachment publishes a lease and exact generation key before building content. Two bounded content workers prepare bases and overlays in the background, with one reconciliation at a time per worktree; traditional content-mode attachment still waits for the content base to initialize.
- Content overlays retain the admission policy and verified path evidence from the last publication. File hints reopen only the affected files; directory hints discover only their subtrees. Deleted or replaced ancestors retire their former members. Ignore-source changes, tracked-file exemption changes, ambiguous case spellings, overflow and periodic repair require full reconciliation. Admission, visibility and evidence publish together; `last_reconcile.metadata_files_checked` counts checkout files verified in that pass. In-memory membership updates and checkpoint persistence still depend on the view size.
- A metadata-only file catalog belongs to each serving registration and shares its watcher. It applies the shared directory exclusions at discovery and includes hidden, binary and large files under the engine's ignore rules without waiting for content admission. `files/page` returns at most 1,024 paths and a membership epoch; a cursor fails after membership changes. `files/refresh` confirms file discovery independently of content readiness. Ordinary file hints repair only their paths and ancestors; directory hints repair subtrees. Ignore changes, new ignore sources, overflow and periodic reconciliation trigger a full walk. `files/fuzzy` ranks the engine-owned catalog using the checksum-locked shared Nucleo source and returns only the bounded best results.
- Opt-in `cancellable` filename requests observe peer disconnect before queued work, during metadata discovery, while waiting for catalog repair and during ranking. Aborted walks never publish their partial catalogs. Legacy half-closing clients retain their response semantics. Registration, content refresh and detach retain durable completion and cleanup semantics; blocking filesystem or Git reads finish before their root guard is released.
- Concurrent path attachment and detach share the registration lock. A separate bounded release queue drains final leases outside the repository registration lock and rechecks leases afterward. Final detach waits for all root reads, including discovery and content reconciliation that continued after socket cancellation, before removing the watcher and view. Detach is idempotent for the same view and lease, allowing cleanup retries after a cancelled response without reopening a removed checkout.
- Upstream source changes are made only in Ash's temporary build inputs and recorded in the patch; the sibling tgrep checkout is read-only. The patch extends the upstream shared and single-directory services rather than introducing another daemon.
- To update the source, create `source.tar.gz` with `git archive` at the new exact upstream commit, update `ash-runtime.patch`, refresh the source, patch and shared-source digests, and verify the source build and real-engine integration tests. The archive is a source snapshot, not a platform executable.
